title: Steering Robustness into World Action Models via Mechanistic Interpretability and Optimal Control
action_head: world-action model: diffusion-transformer video-generation backbone that denoises latent actions together with future states
methods: linear separability of activations (hinge loss) between nominal and perturbed rollouts
closed-loop steering by LQR on locally linearised activation dynamics (WA-LQR)
question: Do world-action models represent robustness-relevant perturbations (camera orientation, initial gripper position, image noise) in a linearly separable way, and can that be used to steer them back to success without fine-tuning?
key_findings: Separability is architecture-dependent: Cosmos-Policy and DiT4DiT show clear low-dimensional linear separation of perturbed vs nominal activations; LingBot-VA does not.
Separability predicts steerability: hinge loss correlates negatively with steering gains across models and perturbations.
Cosmos-Policy, camera-orientation perturbation, LIBERO-10, average over 5 task transfers: no steering 46.0% +-4.1, prompt steering 46.7%, ActAdd 49.3%, WA-LQR 59.3% +-4.0.
DiT4DiT: initial-gripper perturbation 65.7% -> 65.8% (ActAdd) -> 71.7% (WA-LQR); Gaussian image noise 15.6% -> 43.3% (ActAdd) -> 48.9% (WA-LQR).
LingBot-VA: no major improvement from steering; open-loop ActAdd often degrades success through over-steering, which closed-loop WA-LQR avoids.
ActAdd is hyperparameter-fragile: under Gaussian noise its gain peaks sharply at one steering scale (gamma = 0.1) and vanishes for smaller or larger values.
Linear directions that work for all scenes and tasks could not be constructed; directions transfer only within discovered task groups.

benchmarks: LIBERO-10 with camera, gripper and noise perturbations
evidence.scale: 30 trials per task (Cosmos-Policy), 20 trials per task (LingBot-VA); 5 task transfers per perturbation
evidence.statistics: partial: +- values reported per cell (appear to be standard errors over trials); no significance tests
evidence.baselines: no steering, prompt steering, open-loop ActAdd

causal_validation: Yes: steering interventions in closed-loop rollouts test whether the separating directions control behavior; separability is used as a prediction that the steering results then confirm or refute per architecture.
closed_loop: Yes, success rates are from closed-loop LIBERO rollouts; WA-LQR is itself a closed-loop controller on activations.
limitations_stated: Limited applicability across tasks and models; requires per-setting mechanistic analysis
No method to predict when tasks share transferable representations
critique: The steering directions are built from rollouts labelled by success or failure under the same perturbation family, so 'steering robustness in' is partly supervised adaptation to a known shift rather than a general robustness mechanism.
Simulation only, single benchmark; the headline 'up to 41%' is a best cell, while the camera-orientation average gain over no steering is 13.3 points.
ActAdd's sharp sensitivity to gamma raises the question of how the scale was chosen and whether it was tuned on evaluation tasks; not reported.
The useful contribution is the negative half: separability as a cheap pre-check that predicts when steering will fail (LingBot-VA).
code: project website and code linked in the paper
one_line: Robustness-relevant perturbations are linearly separable inside some world-action models but not others; where they are, contrastive and LQR-based activation steering raises success under shift, and separability predicts in advance where steering will work.
